Compare gold buyers using the same items, tested purity, weight units, final purchase amount, and payment terms. Ask how diamonds and collectible pieces are considered.

In this guide

  • Compare the offer for the items you actually own
  • Ask for the weight, purity, and offer basis
  • Give jewelry and coins the appropriate evaluation
  • Choose a selling process you can evaluate
  • Arrange large quantities and payment in advance
  • Questions before your first visit

Compare the offer for the items you actually own

Choosing a gold buyer in Downtown Los Angeles starts with a clear evaluation. Ask what was tested, what was weighed, and how those findings affect the final amount. A large advertised price means little if it applies to a different purity, excludes some of your items, or changes after deductions.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys gold jewelry, scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Bring one piece or discuss a substantial collection. Our gold-buying service explains the items we evaluate.

Ask for the weight, purity, and offer basis

A useful comparison identifies the same pieces in each offer. For a mixed lot, ask whether 10K, 14K, 18K, and other purities are recorded separately. Confirm the weight unit and how diamonds, springs, or other components affect the metal weight used.

Karat describes the proportion of gold in an alloy: 14K means 14 parts out of 24. Gold plating and gold-filled construction describe different materials. The FTC guide to jewelry markings explains these distinctions. A visible stamp is a starting point for an examination, rather than a substitute for testing the item.

  • Items included: Are both quotes for the complete lot or only selected pieces?
  • Measured weight: Are the units and treatment of non-gold components clear?
  • Tested purity: Is the buyer explaining different karats and any uncertain components?
  • Net payment: What is the final amount after any stated charges, and how will it be paid?

For the calculation behind an estimate, see how gold is valued. There is no universal payout percentage that establishes a fair offer for every item.

Give jewelry and coins the appropriate evaluation

A broken unbranded chain, a diamond-set Cuban bracelet, and a collectible gold coin need different discussions. Ask whether an item is being considered for its metal, its stones, or resale as a complete piece. Avoid dismantling jewelry or removing diamonds before that discussion.

Bring existing diamond reports, maker documentation, and coin inventory notes with the matching items. Those records help identify what you have; they do not guarantee a premium. Keep potentially collectible coins in their holders and mention any known history.

The World Gold Council's purity and fineness guide is useful when interpreting karat and fineness markings. Our coin-buyer guide covers questions specific to coin collections.

Choose a selling process you can evaluate

An in-person visit lets you ask questions while the buyer examines your property. A mail-in service involves shipping, receipt, an evaluation period, and written acceptance or return terms. Before using either option, establish what happens if you decline an offer and when your property or payment will be returned.

An outright sale also differs from a pawn loan: a loan has repayment terms and the item serves as security. Compare the transaction you actually want. The business category alone does not establish which buyer will make the better offer.

Arrange large quantities and payment in advance

For heavy Cuban chains, substantial scrap lots, or quantities of gold and silver coins, call 310-663-1340 before your visit. Describe the types of items and approximate quantity so the visit and evaluation can be coordinated. Keep separate collections labeled and make your own item list.

Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check. Discuss the method and timing before accepting an offer, especially for a high-value transaction. A bank wire or check may have bank processing or availability times; clarify those details rather than assuming every payment method works identically.

Questions before your first visit

Is a purchase offer the same as an insurance appraisal?

No. A purchase offer states what a buyer is willing to pay. An insurance appraisal serves a different purpose and may use a different value basis. Say what you need before arranging an evaluation.

What if I only want to sell some of the items?

Identify those pieces before accepting. Ask for a revised amount for the selected items, because a quote for a full collection may not apply unchanged to a smaller group.

What should I confirm before traveling to Hill Street?

Confirm your visit time, the items you want evaluated, any requested identification or documents, and your preferred payment method. Our contact page provides the Downtown Los Angeles location and appointment options.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

Gold buying in Downtown Los Angeles · 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

  • FTC: understanding precious-metal jewelry markings
  • World Gold Council: gold purity, karat and fineness

A gold-bracelet offer depends on tested purity, net metal weight, construction, condition, and any diamonds. Bring Cuban links, bangles, and broken pieces for evaluation.

In this guide

  • Selling Cuban bracelets, bangles, and broken gold
  • Why Cuban-link construction matters
  • Evaluate diamond-set bracelets as complete pieces
  • Broken, vintage, and signed bracelets need different attention
  • Compare the final amount for the same bracelets
  • Bring one bracelet or a substantial collection

Selling Cuban bracelets, bangles, and broken gold

A heavy bracelet can contain substantial gold, but its size alone does not establish its value. A useful evaluation considers its tested purity, metal weight, construction, condition, and any diamonds. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys Cuban bracelets with or without diamonds, plain gold bangles, and scrap gold in Downtown Los Angeles.

Bring the complete bracelet, including detached links or a broken clasp. If you have matching chains or other unwanted pieces, they can be discussed together through our gold and jewelry buying service.

Why Cuban-link construction matters

Two bracelets of similar width can have different weights. Hollow links contain less metal than comparable solid links, while clasps and repairs may introduce components that need separate examination. Ask which parts are included in the gold calculation rather than treating the entire scale reading as pure gold.

For example, 14K describes an alloy containing 14 parts gold out of 24; it does not mean every gram of the bracelet is pure gold. A gold-plated or gold-filled item has a different construction from karat-gold jewelry. The FTC's explanation of gold markings and plating helps distinguish these terms.

Keep any purchase receipt that identifies the material, and point out known repairs. If you are also selling a matching chain, our 14K and Cuban-chain guide explains the same weight and construction questions in more detail.

Evaluate diamond-set bracelets as complete pieces

A diamond-set Cuban bracelet needs more than a gold-weight calculation. Ask how the stones are identified and whether their contribution is included in the offer. Total diamond weight across many small stones does not describe the size or quality of any individual diamond.

Diamond quality involves carat weight, color, clarity, and cut, as explained in GIA's diamond quality guide. Bring any existing reports, while recognizing that a report may cover a particular stone rather than every stone in a bracelet.

Do not remove stones yourself. Request an evaluation of the complete bracelet first, then clarify the terms of any proposed disassembly. Our diamond-buying service provides a starting point for discussing significant stones.

Broken, vintage, and signed bracelets need different attention

A broken clasp does not remove the gold already present in a bracelet. For a piece evaluated primarily for metal, tested purity and recoverable gold weight remain central. Damage can nevertheless affect the value of jewelry that might otherwise be resold intact.

Keep maker marks, original boxes, and useful history with a signed or antique bracelet. Do not assume an inherited piece should be sold only as scrap. Ask whether the design, condition, or maker gives the complete item a resale opportunity before authorizing repairs, polishing, or dismantling.

For a mixture of damaged jewelry, single earrings, and detached links, use our scrap-gold preparation guide. Keep separate pieces organized so you can follow the evaluation.

Compare the final amount for the same bracelets

Ask each buyer to identify the pieces, tested karats, weight units, treatment of stones, and net payment. A per-gram quote is only comparable when the material and calculation basis match. An attractive preliminary estimate is not the same as an offer following examination.

There is no single percentage of spot price that proves an offer is fair for every bracelet. A complete jewelry offer can reflect a different resale opportunity from a metal-only purchase. Request an explanation and compare the amount you would receive for the same items.

Bring one bracelet or a substantial collection

Visit Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. We buy heavy Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, scrap gold, gold coins, and silver coins. Large quantities and high-value transactions are welcome.

For a substantial lot, arrange your visit and discuss payment beforehand. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check. Confirm the final amount and payment timing before accepting the purchase.

Should I repair a broken bracelet before selling?

Have it evaluated first. A repair may not add enough to the purchase offer to justify its cost, and a vintage or signed piece may need specialist attention. Bring detached components with the bracelet.

Can I sell a bracelet if I do not know its karat?

Yes, you can bring it for evaluation and explain what is unknown. The buyer needs to establish its material before making a meaningful offer; a photograph or color alone cannot confirm gold content.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

Gold buying in Downtown Los Angeles · 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

  • FTC: understanding precious-metal jewelry markings
  • GIA: diamond quality factors

Estimate 14K gold content using net alloy weight × 14/24, then multiply by the pure-gold price per gram. The result is a metal-content estimate, not a purchase offer.

In this guide

  • Calculate the gold content before comparing prices
  • Convert a troy-ounce reference into grams
  • Worked example: a 25-gram 14K bracelet
  • Understand the difference between a reference and an offer
  • Compare 14K gold offers on the same basis
  • Arrange a 14K gold evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Calculate the gold content before comparing prices

To estimate the metal value of 14K gold, multiply the pure-gold price per gram by 14 ÷ 24, or approximately 0.5833. Then multiply by the net weight of the 14K alloy. This estimates contained gold value; a purchase offer also depends on the actual item and the buyer's terms.

14K means 14 parts gold in a 24-part alloy. A 585 fineness mark indicates 58.5% gold and is commonly associated with 14K jewelry. The World Gold Council's explanation of karat and fineness describes the small distinction between nominal 14K and 585. Use the purity established during the evaluation when comparing a real offer.

Convert a troy-ounce reference into grams

If a gold-price reference is quoted in dollars per troy ounce, first divide it by 31.1034768 to obtain dollars per gram of pure gold. A troy ounce is different from an ordinary household ounce. The NIST mass reference provides the conversion.

Estimated contained gold value = net alloy weight in grams × tested gold fraction × pure-gold price per gram.

The World Gold Council's gold-price data offers market references. Check the currency, unit, date, and whether a displayed value is an average or benchmark. It is not a binding offer for your jewelry, and this article does not display a live buying rate.

Worked example: a 25-gram 14K bracelet

Assume a plain bracelet contains 25 grams of 14K alloy after accounting for any non-gold components. Its estimated pure-gold content is 25 × 14 ÷ 24 = approximately 14.58 grams. Multiply that amount by the current reference price per gram of pure gold to obtain a metal-content estimate.

Net 14K alloy weightApproximate pure gold
10 grams5.83 grams

These are calculated metal quantities, not promised payouts. A bracelet's total weight may also include diamonds, non-gold springs, or other materials. A household scale and a visible stamp can help you prepare questions, but they do not establish a tested net gold weight.

Understand the difference between a reference and an offer

A metal-only purchase offer can reflect testing, processing, refining, resale costs, and the buyer's margin. Jewelry with a desirable maker, significant stones, or collectible features may instead deserve evaluation as a complete piece. Do not add an intact jewelry resale estimate to its full metal value; that could count the same material twice.

For heavy Cuban chains and bracelets, ask about construction as well as weight. Hollow links and solid links can look similar while containing different amounts of metal. If diamonds are present, ask how the stones affect both the weight calculation and the offer. See our 14K chain guide for these item-specific checks.

Compare 14K gold offers on the same basis

Keep the same pieces together when requesting comparisons. Ask each buyer to state the tested purity, weight unit, weight used, whether stones are included, any charges, and the final payment. If one quote uses grams and another uses pennyweights, ask for matching units before comparing rates.

An estimate given before examination may change if the item differs from the description. Compare final amounts for the actual jewelry, not only an advertised per-gram figure. Our gold-valuation guide covers the broader factors behind an offer.

Keep matching pieces and existing reports together. Call 310-663-1340 to discuss a substantial lot and your preferred payment method. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check. Visit our gold-buying page for the full buying scope.

Are equal weights of 14K white and yellow gold worth the same?

At the same tested gold fraction, they contain the same amount of gold. A complete piece's offer may still differ because of its stones, maker, condition, or resale demand. Read more about white gold's alloy and finish.

Should I remove stones before weighing my jewelry?

No. Have the intact jewelry evaluated first and ask how non-gold weight is accounted for. Removing stones can damage the setting and make an evaluation of the complete piece more difficult.

Can this formula tell me the best day to sell?

No. It explains metal content using a stated price reference; it does not predict markets. Decide using an actual offer, the items you own, and your circumstances.

Gold valuation starts with tested purity, net metal weight, and a dated price reference. Stones, condition, and resale potential can also affect an offer.

In this guide

  • What Determines the Value of Gold?
  • What Does Gold Karat Mean?
  • How Do You Identify the Karat of Gold Jewelry?
  • Why Does Gold Weight Matter?
  • What Is a Troy Ounce?
  • What Is the Gold Spot Price?
  • Why Isn’t My 14K Jewelry Worth the Full Gold Spot Price?
  • How Is the Gold Content of Jewelry Estimated?
  • How Do Gold Buyers Test Gold?
  • Does the Condition of Gold Jewelry Affect Its Value?
  • Can Broken Gold Still Be Valuable?
  • Are Diamonds and Gemstones Included in Gold Value?
  • Can Designer Jewelry Be Worth More Than Its Gold Content?
  • How Much Is My Gold Worth Today?
  • How Can I Estimate My Gold’s Value Before Selling?
  • How Can I Get a Better Offer for My Gold?
  • Do Pawn Shops Value Gold Differently?
  • Frequently Asked Questions About Gold Value
  • Get Your Gold Evaluated in Los Angeles

If you’re thinking about selling gold in Los Angeles, one of the first questions you may have is: How is gold valued?

The value of gold jewelry is generally influenced by several factors, including its gold purity, weight, current gold market price, and the type of item being evaluated. Some jewelry may also have additional value because of its brand, craftsmanship, gemstones, condition, or collectibility.

Understanding these factors before you sell can make it easier to evaluate an offer and ask the right questions.

At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, we believe sellers should understand how their valuables are evaluated before deciding whether to sell.

What Determines the Value of Gold?

When evaluating gold, buyers typically consider several important factors.

These include:

  • Gold purity or karat
  • Weight
  • Current gold market price
  • Whether the item is solid gold, plated, or another type of material
  • Refining or resale considerations
  • Condition and design
  • Brand or collectible value
  • Diamonds or other gemstones

For ordinary gold jewelry being purchased primarily for its precious metal content, purity, weight, and the prevailing gold price are especially important.

What Does Gold Karat Mean?

Gold karat describes how much pure gold is contained in an alloy.

Pure gold is 24 karat. Jewelry is often made by combining gold with other metals to improve durability or achieve different colors and characteristics.

The FTC explains that an 18K item consists of 18 parts gold and six parts other metal, while a 14K item consists of 14 parts gold and ten parts other metal.

How Pure Is 24K Gold?

24K represents essentially pure gold.

Because pure gold is relatively soft, jewelry is frequently made using lower

karat alloys rather than 24K gold.

How Pure Is 22K Gold?

22K gold contains approximately 91.7% gold.

It is commonly seen in certain types of jewelry and gold coins.

How Pure Is 18K Gold?

18K gold contains 75% gold.

The remaining 25% consists of other metals used in the alloy.

How Pure Is 14K Gold?

14K gold contains approximately 58.3% gold.

It is one of the commonly encountered gold purities in jewelry.

How Pure Is 10K Gold?

10K gold contains approximately 41.7% gold.

Because the gold percentage is lower than in 14K or 18K jewelry, two items of identical weight can have substantially different gold content.

How Do You Identify the Karat of Gold Jewelry?

Many pieces of jewelry contain a quality mark indicating their gold content.

You may see markings such as:

  • 10K
  • 14K
  • 18K
  • 22K
  • 24K
  • 417
  • 585
  • 750
  • 916

For example, 585 generally corresponds to approximately 58.5% gold, while 750 corresponds to 75% gold.

However, a stamp alone should not always be treated as conclusive proof of an item’s composition.

A professional evaluation may include testing to confirm the actual precious metal content.

The FTC provides consumer guidance about gold quality marks and how they communicate the amount of gold in jewelry.

Why Does Gold Weight Matter?

Once the purity of an item is established, its weight becomes another major part of determining its underlying gold content.

In simple terms, an item containing more actual gold generally has a higher underlying metal value than an otherwise comparable item containing less gold.

However, sellers should understand what exactly is being weighed.

A piece of jewelry may contain:

  • Gold
  • Diamonds
  • Gemstones
  • Clasps
  • Springs
  • Other metals
  • Non metal components

These components can affect how the total weight relates to the actual amount of gold.

What Is a Troy Ounce?

Gold markets commonly quote precious metals using troy ounces, rather than the ordinary avoirdupois ounces Americans commonly use for everyday goods.

One troy ounce is approximately 31.103 grams, according to NIST.

This distinction is important because a standard ounce and a troy ounce are not the same measurement.

You may also encounter gold buyers using grams or pennyweights.

When receiving an evaluation, ask which unit of measurement is being used.

What Is the Gold Spot Price?

The spot price of gold is a market reference for gold.

Gold prices fluctuate as markets change, so the price you see today may differ from the price on another day.

The World Gold Council provides gold spot price information and notes that the gold market also uses benchmarks such as the LBMA Gold Price.

This market price is an important starting point for understanding gold value—but it does not automatically equal the amount a buyer will pay for your jewelry.

Why Isn’t My 14K Jewelry Worth the Full Gold Spot Price?

This is one of the most important concepts for gold sellers to understand.

The quoted gold price generally refers to gold at a specified market standard. Your jewelry may contain considerably less than 100% gold.

For example, 14K jewelry contains roughly 14 parts gold out of 24.

So if you have a 14K bracelet weighing 20 grams, you should not simply multiply all 20 grams by the market price of pure gold per gram and assume that is what a buyer should pay.

The actual gold content first needs to be considered.

The buyer may then account for additional factors involved in purchasing, processing, refining, or reselling the item.

How Is the Gold Content of Jewelry Estimated?

A simplified way of understanding the underlying gold content is:

Net alloy weight × gold purity = approximate pure-gold weight

For example, imagine the gold alloy in a piece weighs 20 grams after accounting for stones and non-gold components, and tests as 18K.

18K gold is 75% gold.

A simplified calculation would therefore be:

20 grams × 75% = approximately 15 grams of gold content

That does not mean the item’s purchase offer will equal the market value of exactly 15 grams of pure gold.

Instead, it helps explain the relationship between the item’s total weight, purity, and underlying precious-metal content.

How Do Gold Buyers Test Gold?

Gold buyers may use different methods depending on the item being evaluated.

Visual Inspection and Hallmarks

An evaluator may first inspect the item for markings indicating karat or fineness.

These markings provide useful information but may still need verification.

Electronic or X-Ray Testing

Some professional buyers use electronic equipment or X-ray fluorescence technology to help analyze metal composition.

Different testing methods have different applications and limitations, which is why an experienced evaluator may use more than one piece of information when determining an item’s composition.

Acid Testing

Acid testing is another traditional method used to help assess gold purity.

The appropriate testing method depends on the type and condition of the item.

If you’re selling gold, you can ask the buyer how your gold was tested and how the purity was determined.

Does the Condition of Gold Jewelry Affect Its Value?

It depends on how the item is being valued.

If a broken chain is being purchased primarily for its precious-metal content, the fact that the chain is broken may matter less than its purity and gold weight.

But some jewelry may have additional resale value when it is:

  • Made by a desirable designer
  • Antique or vintage
  • In excellent condition
  • Rare
  • Collectible
  • Set with valuable gemstones

That is why potentially important jewelry shouldn’t automatically be treated as scrap.

Can Broken Gold Still Be Valuable?

Yes.

A broken gold necklace, damaged bracelet, bent ring, single earring, or other unwanted piece can still contain valuable gold.

Its precious-metal content does not disappear simply because the jewelry can no longer be worn.

If you have broken or unwanted jewelry, having it evaluated can help you understand whether it has precious-metal or additional resale value.

Are Diamonds and Gemstones Included in Gold Value?

Diamonds and gemstones should be considered separately from the gold content when they may have meaningful value.

A piece of jewelry might therefore have several potential components of value:

Consider metal content, stones, and the resale value of the complete piece without counting the same value twice.

Not every stone necessarily has significant secondary-market value, but valuable diamonds or gemstones should not automatically be ignored.

If your jewelry contains diamonds or significant gemstones, ask whether they are being evaluated separately from the gold.

Can Designer Jewelry Be Worth More Than Its Gold Content?

Yes.

Some designer, vintage, antique, collectible, or luxury jewelry can potentially be worth more as a complete piece than simply as precious metal.

Before selling potentially valuable branded jewelry, consider whether the piece has characteristics such as:

  • Recognizable designer markings
  • Original documentation
  • Serial numbers
  • Original boxes
  • Certificates
  • Historical or collectible significance

A knowledgeable evaluator should consider whether an item deserves evaluation beyond its melt or precious-metal value.

How Much Is My Gold Worth Today?

There is no single accurate answer without knowing what you have.

Determining your gold’s potential value requires information such as:

  • Weight
  • Karat or purity
  • Current gold market price
  • Whether the item contains gemstones
  • Brand or maker
  • Condition
  • Potential resale or collectible value

Because the gold market changes, avoid relying on an old article containing a fixed dollar amount for what gold is supposedly “worth today.”

For current market information, the World Gold Council gold-price data provides a useful reference.

How Can I Estimate My Gold’s Value Before Selling?

You can start by looking for the karat mark on your jewelry and getting an approximate weight.

Then check a reputable source for the current gold market price.

However, treat any home calculation as an estimate, not a guaranteed purchase offer.

Professional testing may determine that the item’s actual composition or weight differs from what you expected.

Additionally, jewelry with diamonds, gemstones, designer provenance, or collectible value may require a different type of evaluation.

How Can I Get a Better Offer for My Gold?

The goal shouldn’t simply be finding the buyer making the biggest advertising claim.

Instead, look for a buyer who provides a transparent evaluation.

Before selling:

  • Know what type of gold you have
  • Ask how purity was determined
  • Ask to understand the weight
  • Check the current gold market
  • Ask whether gemstones have separate value
  • Ask whether designer or collectible value was considered
  • Understand the offer before accepting it

If you’re comparing different ways to sell, read our guide Where to Sell Gold in Los Angeles: How to Get the Best Price for Your Gold.

Do Pawn Shops Value Gold Differently?

Different buyers can have different business models, operating costs, resale opportunities, and purchasing criteria.

That means offers for the same item may vary.

If you’re considering a pawn shop, see our guide How Much Do Pawn Shops Pay for Gold? What Los Angeles Sellers Should Know for a more detailed explanation.

Frequently Asked Questions About Gold Value

Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold?

Per equal unit of weight, 18K gold contains more pure gold than 14K gold. However, the total value of a specific piece also depends on its weight and potentially its design, gemstones, brand, condition, and resale value.

Is 14K gold real gold?

Yes. 14K gold is a gold alloy containing 14 parts gold out of 24 total parts. The FTC’s consumer guidance explains how karat markings indicate the proportion of gold in jewelry.

Is broken gold worth less?

If an item is being valued primarily for its precious-metal content, being broken does not eliminate the value of the gold it contains. A wearable or collectible piece, however, may have additional value based on condition.

Do gold prices change every day?

Gold prices fluctuate with market activity. For that reason, the reference price used when evaluating gold can change over time. The World Gold Council maintains gold spot-price data and related market information.

Should I sell gold based only on its weight?

No. Weight is only one part of the evaluation. Purity is crucial, and some jewelry can also have value from diamonds, gemstones, brand, craftsmanship, rarity, or collectibility.

How do I know whether a gold offer is fair?

Ask the buyer to explain the item’s tested purity, weight, market-price reference, and any other factors used in calculating the offer. Understanding those components makes comparing evaluations easier.

There should be no mystery about the basic factors affecting your gold’s value.

Stones, condition, and resale potential can also affect an offer.Heavy Cuban-link chains, bangles and mixed gold jewelry piled on black velvet.In this guideWhat Determines the Value of Gold?What Does Gold Karat Mean?How Do You Identify the Karat of Gold Jewelry?Why Does Gold Weight Matter?What Is a Troy Ounce?What Is the Gold Spot Price?Why Isn’t My 14K Jewelry Worth the Full Gold Spot Price?How Is the Gold Content of Jewelry Estimated?How Do Gold Buyers Test Gold?Does the Condition of Gold Jewelry Affect Its Value?Can Broken Gold Still Be Valuable?Are Diamonds and Gemstones Included in Gold Value?Can Designer Jewelry Be Worth More Than Its Gold Content?How Much Is My Gold Worth Today?How Can I Estimate My Gold’s Value Before Selling?How Can I Get a Better Offer for My Gold?Do Pawn Shops Value Gold Differently?Frequently Asked Questions About Gold ValueGet Your Gold Evaluated in Los Angeles If you’re thinking about selling gold in Los Angeles, one of the first questions you may have is: How is gold valued? The value of gold jewelry is generally influenced by several factors, including its gold purity, weight, current gold market price, and the type of item being evaluated. Some jewelry may also have additional value because of its brand, craftsmanship, gemstones, condition, or collectibility. Understanding these factors before you sell can make it easier to evaluate an offer and ask the right questions. At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, we believe sellers should understand how their valuables are evaluated before deciding whether to sell. What Determines the Value of Gold? When evaluating gold, buyers typically consider several important factors. These include: Gold purity or karat Weight Current gold market price Whether the item is solid gold, plated, or another type of material Refining or resale considerations Condition and design Brand or collectible value Diamonds or other gemstones For ordinary gold jewelry being purchased primarily for its precious metal content, purity, weight, and the prevailing gold price are especially important. What Does Gold Karat Mean? Gold karat describes how much pure gold is contained in an alloy. Pure gold is 24 karat. Jewelry is often made by combining gold with other metals to improve durability or achieve different colors and characteristics. The FTC explains that an 18K item consists of 18 parts gold and six parts other metal, while a 14K item consists of 14 parts gold and ten parts other metal. How Pure Is 24K Gold? 24K represents essentially pure gold. Because pure gold is relatively soft, jewelry is frequently made using lower karat alloys rather than 24K gold. How Pure Is 22K Gold? 22K gold contains approximately 91.7% gold. It is commonly seen in certain types of jewelry and gold coins. How Pure Is 18K Gold? 18K gold contains 75% gold. The remaining 25% consists of other metals used in the alloy. How Pure Is 14K Gold? 14K gold contains approximately 58.3% gold. It is one of the commonly encountered gold purities in jewelry. How Pure Is 10K Gold? 10K gold contains approximately 41.7% gold. Because the gold percentage is lower than in 14K or 18K jewelry, two items of identical weight can have substantially different gold content. How Do You Identify the Karat of Gold Jewelry? Many pieces of jewelry contain a quality mark indicating their gold content. You may see markings such as: 10K 14K 18K 22K 24K 417 585 750 916 For example, 585 generally corresponds to approximately 58.5% gold, while 750 corresponds to 75% gold. However, a stamp alone should not always be treated as conclusive proof of an item’s composition. A professional evaluation may include testing to confirm the actual precious metal content. The FTC provides consumer guidance about gold quality marks and how they communicate the amount of gold in jewelry. Why Does Gold Weight Matter? Once the purity of an item is established, its weight becomes another major part of determining its underlying gold content. In simple terms, an item containing more actual gold generally has a higher underlying metal value than an otherwise comparable item containing less gold. However, sellers should understand what exactly is being weighed. A piece of jewelry may contain: Gold Diamonds Gemstones Clasps Springs Other metals Non metal components These components can affect how the total weight relates to the actual amount of gold. What Is a Troy Ounce? Gold markets commonly quote precious metals using troy ounces, rather than the ordinary avoirdupois ounces Americans commonly use for everyday goods. One troy ounce is approximately 31.103 grams, according to NIST. This distinction is important because a standard ounce and a troy ounce are not the same measurement. You may also encounter gold buyers using grams or pennyweights. When receiving an evaluation, ask which unit of measurement is being used. What Is the Gold Spot Price? The spot price of gold is a market reference for gold. Gold prices fluctuate as markets change, so the price you see today may differ from the price on another day. The World Gold Council provides gold spot price information and notes that the gold market also uses benchmarks such as the LBMA Gold Price. This market price is an important starting point for understanding gold value—but it does not automatically equal the amount a buyer will pay for your jewelry. Why Isn’t My 14K Jewelry Worth the Full Gold Spot Price? This is one of the most important concepts for gold sellers to understand. The quoted gold price generally refers to gold at a specified market standard. Your jewelry may contain considerably less than 100% gold. For example, 14K jewelry contains roughly 14 parts gold out of 24. So if you have a 14K bracelet weighing 20 grams, you should not simply multiply all 20 grams by the market price of pure gold per gram and assume that is what a buyer should pay. The actual gold content first needs to be considered. The buyer may then account for additional factors involved in purchasing, processing, refining, or reselling the item. How Is the Gold Content of Jewelry Estimated? A simplified way of understanding the underlying gold content is: Net alloy weight × gold purity = approximate pure-gold weight For example, imagine the gold alloy in a piece weighs 20 grams after accounting for stones and non-gold components, and tests as 18K. 18K gold is 75% gold. A simplified calculation would therefore be: 20 grams × 75% = approximately 15 grams of gold content That does not mean the item’s purchase offer will equal the market value of exactly 15 grams of pure gold. Instead, it helps explain the relationship between the item’s total weight, purity, and underlying precious-metal content. How Do Gold Buyers Test Gold? Gold buyers may use different methods depending on the item being evaluated. Visual Inspection and Hallmarks An evaluator may first inspect the item for markings indicating karat or fineness. These markings provide useful information but may still need verification. Electronic or X-Ray Testing Some professional buyers use electronic equipment or X-ray fluorescence technology to help analyze metal composition. Different testing methods have different applications and limitations, which is why an experienced evaluator may use more than one piece of information when determining an item’s composition. Acid Testing Acid testing is another traditional method used to help assess gold purity. The appropriate testing method depends on the type and condition of the item. If you’re selling gold, you can ask the buyer how your gold was tested and how the purity was determined. Does the Condition of Gold Jewelry Affect Its Value? It depends on how the item is being valued.Gold jewelry arranged beside a digital scale and testing tools. If a broken chain is being purchased primarily for its precious-metal content, the fact that the chain is broken may matter less than its purity and gold weight. But some jewelry may have additional resale value when it is: Made by a desirable designer Antique or vintage In excellent condition Rare Collectible Set with valuable gemstones That is why potentially important jewelry shouldn’t automatically be treated as scrap. Can Broken Gold Still Be Valuable? Yes. A broken gold necklace, damaged bracelet, bent ring, single earring, or other unwanted piece can still contain valuable gold. Its precious-metal content does not disappear simply because the jewelry can no longer be worn. If you have broken or unwanted jewelry, having it evaluated can help you understand whether it has precious-metal or additional resale value. Are Diamonds and Gemstones Included in Gold Value? Diamonds and gemstones should be considered separately from the gold content when they may have meaningful value. A piece of jewelry might therefore have several potential components of value: Consider metal content, stones, and the resale value of the complete piece without counting the same value twice. Not every stone necessarily has significant secondary-market value, but valuable diamonds or gemstones should not automatically be ignored. If your jewelry contains diamonds or significant gemstones, ask whether they are being evaluated separately from the gold. Can Designer Jewelry Be Worth More Than Its Gold Content? Yes. Some designer, vintage, antique, collectible, or luxury jewelry can potentially be worth more as a complete piece than simply as precious metal. Before selling potentially valuable branded jewelry, consider whether the piece has characteristics such as: Recognizable designer markings Original documentation Serial numbers Original boxes Certificates Historical or collectible significance A knowledgeable evaluator should consider whether an item deserves evaluation beyond its melt or precious-metal value. How Much Is My Gold Worth Today? There is no single accurate answer without knowing what you have. Determining your gold’s potential value requires information such as: Weight Karat or purity Current gold market price Whether the item contains gemstones Brand or maker Condition Potential resale or collectible value Because the gold market changes, avoid relying on an old article containing a fixed dollar amount for what gold is supposedly “worth today.” For current market information, the World Gold Council gold-price data provides a useful reference. How Can I Estimate My Gold’s Value Before Selling? You can start by looking for the karat mark on your jewelry and getting an approximate weight. Then check a reputable source for the current gold market price. However, treat any home calculation as an estimate, not a guaranteed purchase offer. Professional testing may determine that the item’s actual composition or weight differs from what you expected. Additionally, jewelry with diamonds, gemstones, designer provenance, or collectible value may require a different type of evaluation. How Can I Get a Better Offer for My Gold? The goal shouldn’t simply be finding the buyer making the biggest advertising claim. Instead, look for a buyer who provides a transparent evaluation. Before selling: Know what type of gold you have Ask how purity was determined Ask to understand the weight Check the current gold market Ask whether gemstones have separate value Ask whether designer or collectible value was considered Understand the offer before accepting it If you’re comparing different ways to sell, read our guide Where to Sell Gold in Los Angeles: How to Get the Best Price for Your Gold. Do Pawn Shops Value Gold Differently? Different buyers can have different business models, operating costs, resale opportunities, and purchasing criteria. That means offers for the same item may vary. If you’re considering a pawn shop, see our guide How Much Do Pawn Shops Pay for Gold? What Los Angeles Sellers Should Know for a more detailed explanation. Frequently Asked Questions About Gold Value Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold? Per equal unit of weight, 18K gold contains more pure gold than 14K gold. However, the total value of a specific piece also depends on its weight and potentially its design, gemstones, brand, condition, and resale value. Is 14K gold real gold? Yes. 14K gold is a gold alloy containing 14 parts gold out of 24 total parts. The FTC’s consumer guidance explains how karat markings indicate the proportion of gold in jewelry. Is broken gold worth less? If an item is being valued primarily for its precious-metal content, being broken does not eliminate the value of the gold it contains. A wearable or collectible piece, however, may have additional value based on condition. Do gold prices change every day? Gold prices fluctuate with market activity. For that reason, the reference price used when evaluating gold can change over time. The World Gold Council maintains gold spot-price data and related market information. Should I sell gold based only on its weight? No. Weight is only one part of the evaluation. Purity is crucial, and some jewelry can also have value from diamonds, gemstones, brand, craftsmanship, rarity, or collectibility. How do I know whether a gold offer is fair? Ask the buyer to explain the item’s tested purity, weight, market-price reference, and any other factors used in calculating the offer. Understanding those components makes comparing evaluations easier. Get Your Gold Evaluated in Los Angeles Understanding how gold is valued can help you make a more informed decision before selling. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates gold jewelry and other valuables for customers in Los Angeles. If you have gold jewelry, broken gold, coins, bullion, estate jewelry, diamonds, or other valuables, bring the items in for an evaluation and ask questions about how their value is determined. There should be no mystery about the basic factors affecting your gold’s value.
